primary_decision.reason: price context and historical-volume activity did not improve probabilistic direction detection portably, and every cost-aware directional policy lost after 5 bps per side

population.surface: two fixed non-overlapping clocks per complete stock-session with no setup, loop, regime, or direction filter

target.long: upper causal-scale barrier uniquely touched first
target.short: lower causal-scale barrier uniquely touched first
target.neutral: neither touched within 24 bars or first interaction unresolvable within one five-minute bar
target.barrier_bps: clip(4 * prior-12-bar median true range bps, 40, 250)

main_findings: Long, short, and neutral form a meaningful output vocabulary; the target was not degenerate because both directional classes had substantial support.
The one-shot price equation mainly learned the neutral base rate and failed to identify which side would touch first.
Small macro-F1 gains came from rare directional class predictions, but log loss worsened and directional precision remained low.
The cost-aware probability-margin equation emitted many directions, but realised precision stayed near the unconditional class rates and losses were securely negative.
Historical-volume activity did not provide a portable incremental direction signal.
Loops were not needed to reach this negative result and remain excluded from the primary directional detector.

next_hypothesis.name: dynamic_competing_first_touch_hazards
next_hypothesis.reason: static direction context failed while earlier completed-path research contained the strongest available occurrence-level information
next_hypothesis.equation: separate causal upper-touch and lower-touch hazards plus survival/neutral probability, updated after every completed bar
next_hypothesis.state_rule: emit long or short only when its lower expected-net uncertainty bound is positive; otherwise neutral/unknown
